¶
'''Amphipyleæ''' (am-fi-pil′ẹ̄-ē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < Gr. ἀμφίπυλος, with two entrances, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + πύλη, a gate, entrance.] A division of ''Phæodaria'' (which see), containing those phæodarians which have pseudopodal openings at the opposite poles of the central capsule: distinguished from ''Monopyleæ''. ''Haeckel.''

'''amphipylean''' (am″fi-pi-lē′ạn), ''a.'' Of or pertaining to the ''Amphipyleæ.''

'''Amphirhina''' (am-fi-rī′nä̤), ''n. pl.'' [NL., neut. pl. of ''amphirhinus'': see ''amphirhine.''] A prime division of the skulled vertebrates, or ''Craniota'', including all except the ''Monorhina'' (which see); the double-breathers. {{smaller|It is a term expressive rather of an evolutionary series of animals than of a definite zoölogical division.}}

'''amphirhine''' (am′fi-rin), ''a.'' [< NL. ''amphirhinus'', < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + ῥίς, ῥίν, nose.] Double-nostriled: specifically said of the ''Amphirhina.''
{{smaller block|Should jaws be absent, the Cephalaspidæ would approach the Marsipobranchii more nearly than any of the other ''amphirhine'' fishes do.
{{right|''Huxley'', Anat. Vert., p. 129.}}}}

'''amphisarca''' (am-fi-sär′kä̤), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + σάρξ (σαρκ-), flesh.] Any hard-rinded fruit having a succulent interior and a crustaceous or woody exterior, as the gourd.
readings.c1s3:
[Rare.]

'''amphisaurid''' (am-fi-sâ′rid), ''n.'' A dinosaurian reptile of the family ''Amphisauridæ.''

'''Amphisauridæ''' (am-fi-sâ′ri-dē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Amphisaurus'' + ''-idæ.''] A family of dinosaurian reptiles: now superseded by ''Anchisauridæ.''

'''Amphisaurus''' (am-fi-sâ′rus), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + σαῦρος, lizard.] A genus of dinosaurian reptiles with amphicœlous vertebræ. The name is now superseded by ''Anchisaurus,'' and is a synonym of ''Megadactylus'' of Hitchcock.

'''amphisbæna''' (am-fis-bē′nä̤), ''n.'' [Early mod. E. ''amphibene,'' ME. corruptly ''alphibena,'' = OF. ''amphisbeine,'' mod. F. ''amphisbène'' = Sp. ''anfisbena, anfisibena'' = Pg. ''amphisbena'' = It. ''anfisbena, anfesibena,'' < L. ''amphisbæna,'' < Gr. ἀμφίσβαινα, a kind of serpent believed to move with either end foremost, < ἀμφίς, at both ends, a form of ἀμφί (see ''amphi-''), + βαίνειν, go, = L. ''venire,'' come, = E. ''come.''] '''1.''' A fabulous venomous serpent supposed to have a head at each end and to be able to move in either direction.
{{smaller block|<poem>Complicated monsters head and tail,
Scorpion, and asp, and ''amphisbæna'' dire,
Cerastes horn’d, hydrus, and elops drear,
And dipsas.</poem>
{{right|''Milton,'' P. L., x. 524.}}
<poem>Two vipers of one breed — an ''amphisbæna,''
Each end a sting.</poem>
{{right|''Tennyson,'' Queen Mary, iii. 4.}}}}

'''Amphisbænoidæa''' (am″fis-bẹ̄-noi′dẹ̄-ä̤), ''n. pl.'' Same as ''Amphisbænoida''.

'''amphisbænous''' (am-fis-bē′nus), ''a.'' Same as ''amphisbænic''.

'''amphiscian''' (am-fish′i-a̤n), ''n.'' One of the amphiscii.

'''amphiscii''' (am-fish′i-ī), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < Gr. ἀμφίσκιος, pl. ἀμφίσκιοι, throwing a shadow both ways, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + σκιά, shadow. Cf. ''antiscii''.] In ''geog.'', the inhabitants of the intertropical regions, whose shadows at noon are cast in one part of the year to the north and in the other part to the south, according as the sun is in the southern or the northern signs.

'''amphisien†''', ''a.'' [For ''amphiscien'' = E. ''amphiscian'', as adj.] In ''her.'', double; having two heads.

'''Amphisile''' (am-fis′i-lē), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί or ἀμφίς, around; it is uncertain what the last two syllables were intended to represent.] A genus of fishes, typical of the family ''Amphisilidæ'', formerly referred to the sea-snipes, ''Fistulariidæ'' or ''Aulostomidæ'', and by Günther to the ''Centriscidæ''.

'''amphistomid''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mid), ''n.'' One of the ''Amphistomidæ.''

'''Amphistomidæ''' (am-fi-stom′i-dē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Amphistomum'' + ''-idæ.''] A family of trematode

'''amphistomoid''' (am-fis′tọ̄-moid), ''a.'' [< ''Amphistomum'' + ''-oid.''] Of or pertaining to the family ''Amphistomidæ''; amphistomous.

'''amphistomous''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mus), ''a.'' [< NL. ''amphistomus'', < Gr. ἀμφίστομος, with double mouth, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + στόμα, mouth: see ''stoma.''] Having a mouth-like orifice at either end of the body, by which to adhere to the intestines of animals, as some trematode parasitic worms; amphistomoid.

'''Amphistomum''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mum), ''n.'' [NL., neut. of ''amphistomus'', with double mouth: see ''amphistomous.''] A genus of trematode parasitic worms, typical of the family ''Amphistomidæ.''

'''amphistylic''' (am-fi-stī′lik), ''a.'' [< Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + στῦλος, a pillar: see ''style''<sup>2</sup>.] Having pillars on both sides: applied in ''zoöl.'' to the skulls of sharks, which have supports for both the upper and lower mandibular arches. ''Huxley.''

'''amphitheater, amphitheatre''' (am-fi-thē′a̤-tėr), ''n.'' [The latter spelling is now usual in England, after the F., though formerly ''amphitheater''; cf. F. ''amphithéâtre'' = Pg. ''amphitheatro'' = Sp. It. ''anfiteatro'' = D. G. ''amphitheater'' = Dan. ''amfiteater'', < L. ''amphitheatrum'', < Gr. ἀμφιθέατρον, prop. neut. of ἀμφιθέατρος, having a theater

'''amphitheatral''' (am-fi-thē′a̤-tra̤l), ''a.'' [< L. ''amphitheatralis'', < ''amphitheatrum'', amphitheater: see ''amphitheater''.] Same as ''amphitheatrical''.

'''amphitheatre,''' ''n.'' See ''amphitheater''.

'''amphitheatric''' (am″fi-thẹ̄-at′rik), ''a.'' Same as ''amphitheatrical''.

'''amphitheatrical''' (am″fi-thẹ̄-at′ri-ka̤l), ''a.'' [< L. ''amphitheatricus'', < ''amphitheatrum'': see ''amphitheater''.] '''1.''' Of, pertaining to, or resembling an amphitheater.
{{smaller block|The first impression on seeing the . . . great ''amphitheatrical'' depressions is, that they have been hollowed out, like other valleys, by the action of water.
{{right|''Darwin'', Voyage of Beagle, II. 225.}}}}
'''2.''' Taking place or exhibited in an amphitheater: as, ''amphitheatrical'' contests.

<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="transcriber" />{{RunningHeader|amphipodous|185|amphitheatrical}}</noinclude>cifically, of or pertaining to the ''Amphipoda.'' Equivalent forms are ''amphipod, amphipodal, amphipodan.''

'''Amphiporidæ''' (am-fi-por′i-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphiporus'' + ''-idæ.'']   In ''zoöl.'', a family of rhynchocœlous turbellarians or nemerteans having the proboscis armed with stylets, which are wanting in the other ''Rhynchocœla.'' Also called ''Enopla.''

'''Amphiporus''' (am-fip′ọ̄-rus), ''n.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + πόρος, passage, pore.]   A genus of nemerteans, typical of the family ''Amphiporidæ'' (which see). {{smaller|''A. lactiflorus'' is a European species, 3 or 4 inches long, found under stones from the North Sea to the Mediterranean.}}

'''amphiprostylar''' (am″fi-prō-stī′lä̤r), ''a.'' Same as ''amphiprostyle.''

'''amphiprostyle''' (am-fi-prō′stīl), ''a.''   [< L. ''amphiprostylos'', < Gr. ἀμφιπρόστυλος, having a prostyle at both ends, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + πρόστυλος, prostyle: see ''prostyle.'']   Literally, having columns both in front and behind. {{smaller|In ''arch.'', ap-}}
{{smaller|plied to a structure having the plan of an ancient Greek or Roman rectangular temple with a portico at each end or in both front and rear, but no columns on the sides or flanks.}}

[[File:century v01 p0211 c1f1.png|center|250px]]
{{c|{{smaller|Plan of Amphiprostyle Temple.}}}}

'''Amphipyleæ''' (am-fi-pil′ẹ̄-ē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφίπυλος, with two entrances, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + πύλη, a gate, entrance.]   A division of ''Phæodaria'' (which see), containing those phæodarians which have pseudopodal openings at the opposite poles of the central capsule: distinguished from ''Monopyleæ''.   ''Haeckel.''

'''amphipylean''' (am″fi-pi-lē′ạn), ''a.'' Of or pertaining to the ''Amphipyleæ.''

'''Amphirhina''' (am-fi-rī′nä̤), ''n. pl.''   [NL., neut. pl. of ''amphirhinus'': see ''amphirhine.'']   A prime division of the skulled vertebrates, or ''Craniota'', including all except the ''Monorhina'' (which see); the double-breathers. {{smaller|It is a term expressive rather of an evolutionary series of animals than of a definite zoölogical division.}}

'''amphirhine''' (am′fi-rin), ''a.''   [< NL. ''amphirhinus'', < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + ῥίς, ῥίν, nose.]   Double-nostriled: specifically said of the ''Amphirhina.''
{{smaller block|Should jaws be absent, the Cephalaspidæ would approach the Marsipobranchii more nearly than any of the other ''amphirhine'' fishes do.
{{right|''Huxley'', Anat. Vert., p. 129.}}}}

'''amphisarca''' (am-fi-sär′kä̤), ''n.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + σάρξ (σαρκ-), flesh.]   Any hard-rinded fruit having a succulent interior and a crustaceous or woody exterior, as the gourd. [Rare.]

'''amphisaurid''' (am-fi-sâ′rid), ''n.'' A dinosaurian reptile of the family ''Amphisauridæ.''

'''Amphisauridæ''' (am-fi-sâ′ri-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphisaurus'' + ''-idæ.'']   A family of dinosaurian reptiles: now superseded by ''Anchisauridæ.''

'''Amphisaurus''' (am-fi-sâ′rus), ''n.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + σαῦρος, lizard.]   A genus of dinosaurian reptiles with amphicœlous vertebræ. The name is now superseded by ''Anchisaurus,'' and is a synonym of ''Megadactylus'' of Hitchcock.

'''amphisbæna''' (am-fis-bē′nä̤), ''n.''   [Early mod. E. ''amphibene,'' ME. corruptly ''alphibena,'' = OF. ''amphisbeine,'' mod. F. ''amphisbène'' = Sp. ''anfisbena, anfisibena'' = Pg. ''amphisbena'' = It. ''anfisbena, anfesibena,'' < L. ''amphisbæna,'' < Gr. ἀμφίσβαινα, a kind of serpent believed to move with either end foremost, < ἀμφίς, at both ends, a form of ἀμφί (see ''amphi-''), + βαίνειν, go, = L. ''venire,'' come, = E. ''come.'']   '''1.''' A fabulous venomous serpent supposed to have a head at each end and to be able to move in either direction.
{{smaller block|<poem>Complicated monsters head and tail,
Scorpion, and asp, and ''amphisbæna'' dire,
Cerastes horn’d, hydrus, and elops drear,
And dipsas.</poem>
{{right|''Milton,'' P. L., x. 524.}}}}
{{smaller block|<poem>Two vipers of one breed — an ''amphisbæna,''
Each end a sting.</poem>
{{right|''Tennyson,'' Queen Mary, iii. 4.}}}} '''2.''' [''cap.''] [NL.] A genus of lizards distinguished by the obtuseness of the head and tail, typical of the family ''Amphisbænidæ.'' {{smaller|The species, inhabiting tropical South America and the West Indies, are}} {{img float|file=century v01 p0211 c1f2.png|width=223px|align=right|cap={{smaller|''Amphisbæna fuliginosa.''}} sluggish and mostly nocturnal, of snake-like aspect from the absence of limbs, and able to move either backward or forward.}}

'''Amphisbænia''' (am-fis-bē′ni-ä̤), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphisbæna.'']   A superfamily group of lacertilians: a synonym of ''Amphisbænoida.''

'''amphisbænian''' (am-fis-bē′ni-a̤n), ''a.'' and ''n.''   [< ''amphisbæna'' + ''-ian.'']   '''I.''' ''a.'' Of or pertaining to the amphisbæna, or to the ''Amphisbænoida.''

'''II.''' ''n.'' Same as ''amphisbæna'', 1.

'''amphisbænic''' (am-fis-bē′nik), ''a.''   [< ''amphisbæna'' + ''-ic.'']   Like the amphisbæna; moving backward or forward with equal ease. An equivalent form is ''amphisbænous.''
{{smaller block|Yoked to it by an ''amphisbænic'' snake.
{{right|''Shelley'', Prom. Unbound, iii. 4.}}}}

'''amphisbænid''' (am-fis-bē′nid), ''n.'' A lizard of the family ''Amphisbænidæ.''

'''Amphisbænidæ''' (am-fis-bē′ni-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphisbæna'' + ''-idæ.'']   The typical family of the group ''Amphisbænoida.'' {{smaller|It embraces sluggish and mostly nocturnal snake-like lizards, such as those of the genus ''Amphisbæna'', which are limbless, and are thus distinguished from the ''Chirotidæ'' (which see).}}

'''Amphisbænoida''' (am″fis-bẹ̄-noi′dä), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphisbæna'' + ''-oida.'']   One of the major divisions of existing ''Lacertilia'' (lizards), differing from all others except the ''Chamæleonida'' in the absence of a columella and of an interorbital septum of the skull. {{smaller|The position of the quadrate bone is peculiar; the skull in general resembles that of an ophidian; the vertebræ are procœlous, and have neither zygantrum nor zygosphene; there is no sacrum; and all but one or two of the precaudal vertebræ bear ribs. The bodies of these lizards are completely snake-like. All the representatives of the group are limbless, excepting members of the genus ''Chirotes'', which have a pair of small pectoral limbs. The tail is extremely short, so that the vent is near the end of the body. The integument is not scaly.}}

'''Amphisbænoidæa''' (am″fis-bẹ̄-noi′dẹ̄-ä̤), ''n. pl.'' Same as ''Amphisbænoida''.

'''amphisbænous''' (am-fis-bē′nus), ''a.'' Same as ''amphisbænic''.

'''amphiscian''' (am-fish′i-a̤n), ''n.'' One of the amphiscii.

'''amphiscii''' (am-fish′i-ī), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφίσκιος, pl. ἀμφίσκιοι, throwing a shadow both ways, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + σκιά, shadow. Cf. ''antiscii''.]   In ''geog.'', the inhabitants of the intertropical regions, whose shadows at noon are cast in one part of the year to the north and in the other part to the south, according as the sun is in the southern or the northern signs.

'''amphisien†''', ''a.''   [For ''amphiscien'' = E. ''amphiscian'', as adj.]   In ''her.'', double; having two heads.

'''Amphisile''' (am-fis′i-lē), ''n.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί or ἀμφίς, around; it is uncertain what the last two syllables were intended to represent.]   A genus of fishes, typical of the family ''Amphisilidæ'', formerly referred to the sea-snipes, ''Fistulariidæ'' or ''Aulostomidæ'', and by Günther to the ''Centriscidæ''.

'''amphisilid''' (am-fis′i-lid), ''n.'' A fish of the family ''Amphisilidæ.''

'''Amphisilidæ''' (am-fi-sil′i-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphisile'' + ''-idæ.'']   A family of hemibranchiate fishes. {{smaller|The body is much compressed, and is armed with bony plates connate with the vertebræ and spinous processes; the tail is deflected downward by the extension of the armature behind. Fishes of this family have an elongated tubiform snout, abdominal ventrals with a spine}}
{{smaller|and several rays, and a dorsal fin crowded out of place by the extension of the dermal armature. It is a most remarkable type, and exceptional among fishes on account of the peculiar development of the skeleton as a sort of shell around the body. The body is almost transparent, and the organs, especially the air-bladder, can be distinctly seen through it. The habits of the family are unknown. Several species inhabit the high seas.}}

[[File:century v01 p0211 c2f1.png|center|345px]]
{{c|{{smaller|''Amphisile scutata.''}}}}

'''amphismela''' (am-fis-mē′lä̤), ''n.''   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφίς, on both sides, + μήλη, a surgical instrument, a probe.]   A double-edged surgical knife.

'''amphispermium''' (am-fi-spėr′mi-um), ''n.''; pl. ''amphispermia'' (-ä̤).   [NL., < Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + σπέρμα, seed.]   In ''bot.'', a term proposed for an indehiscent one-seeded pericarp; an achenium.

'''amphistome''' (am′fi-stōm), ''n.''   [< NL. ''Amphistomum.'']   An animal of the genus ''Amphistomum'' or family ''Amphistomidæ.''

'''amphistomid''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mid), ''n.'' One of the ''Amphistomidæ.''

'''Amphistomidæ''' (am-fi-stom′i-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Amphistomum'' + ''-idæ.'']   A family of trematode worms, of which the genus ''Amphistomum'' is the type. Other genera are ''Diplostomum'' and ''Gastrodiscus.''

'''amphistomoid''' (am-fis′tọ̄-moid), ''a.''   [< ''Amphistomum'' + ''-oid.'']   Of or pertaining to the family ''Amphistomidæ''; amphistomous.

'''amphistomous''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mus), ''a.''   [< NL. ''amphistomus'', < Gr. ἀμφίστομος, with double mouth, < ἀμφί, on both sides, + στόμα, mouth: see ''stoma.'']   Having a mouth-like orifice at either end of the body, by which to adhere to the intestines of animals, as some trematode parasitic worms; amphistomoid.

'''Amphistomum''' (am-fis′tọ̄-mum), ''n.''   [NL., neut. of ''amphistomus'', with double mouth: see ''amphistomous.'']   A genus of trematode parasitic worms, typical of the family ''Amphistomidæ.''

'''amphistylic''' (am-fi-stī′lik), ''a.''   [< Gr. ἀμφί, on both sides, + στῦλος, a pillar: see ''style''<sup>2</sup>.]   Having pillars on both sides: applied in ''zoöl.'' to the skulls of sharks, which have supports for both the upper and lower mandibular arches.   ''Huxley.''

'''amphitheater, amphitheatre''' (am-fi-thē′a̤-tėr), ''n.''   [The latter spelling is now usual in England, after the F., though formerly ''amphitheater''; cf. F. ''amphithéâtre'' = Pg. ''amphitheatro'' = Sp. It. ''anfiteatro'' = D. G. ''amphitheater'' = Dan. ''amfiteater'', < L. ''amphitheatrum'', < Gr. ἀμφιθέατρον, prop. neut. of ἀμφιθέατρος, having a theater (semicircular structure) on both sides, < ἀμφί, around, + θέατρον, a place for seeing shows, a theater: see ''amphi-'' and ''theater''.]   '''1.''' In ''anc. Rom. arch.'', an edifice devoted to the exhibition of gladiatorial contests and the combats of wild beasts. {{smaller|Such edifices were elliptical in form, and consisted of a central area or arena, surrounded by a wall, from which, sloping upward and outward, were rows of seats for the spectators. The earliest amphitheaters were made of wood; the first built of stone date from the time of Augustus. The Colosseum or Flavian amphitheater at Rome was the largest of all the ancient amphitheaters, being capable of containing from 80,000 to 90,000 persons. Those at Nimes and Verona are among the best examples remaining. The dimensions of the latter are 505½ by 403 feet, with a height of 100 feet.}}

[[File:century v01 p0211 c3f1.png|center|310px]]
{{c|{{smaller|Remains of Amphitheater of Arles, France.}}}}

[[File:century v01 p0211 c3f2.png|center|298px]]
{{c|{{smaller|Remains of Amphitheater of Nîmes, France.}}}}

'''2.''' Anything resembling an amphitheater in form, as an oval or circular building with seats rising behind and above each other around a central open space, or a natural area surrounded by rising ground; in ''hort.'', a sloping arrangement of shrubs and trees.
{{smaller block|He surveys all the Wonders in this immense ''Amphitheatre'' that lie between both the Poles of Heaven. {{right|''Addison'', Spectator, No. 315.}}}}

'''3.''' The uppermost gallery of a modern theater.

'''amphitheatral''' (am-fi-thē′a̤-tra̤l), ''a.''   [< L. ''amphitheatralis'', < ''amphitheatrum'', amphitheater: see ''amphitheater''.]   Same as ''amphitheatrical''.

'''amphitheatre,''' ''n.'' See ''amphitheater''.

'''amphitheatric''' (am″fi-thẹ̄-at′rik), ''a.'' Same as ''amphitheatrical''.

'''amphitheatrical''' (am″fi-thẹ̄-at′ri-ka̤l), ''a.''   [< L. ''amphitheatricus'', < ''amphitheatrum'': see ''amphitheater''.]   '''1.''' Of, pertaining to, or resembling an amphitheater.
{{smaller block|The first impression on seeing the . . . great ''amphitheatrical'' depressions is, that they have been hollowed out, like other valleys, by the action of water.
{{right|''Darwin'', Voyage of Beagle, II. 225.}}}}
'''2.''' Taking place or exhibited in an amphitheater: as, ''amphitheatrical'' contests.<noinclude><references/></noinclude>
